record.original_question: Deterministic Minami Perturbation: Minami showed that if $A$ is $n x n$ Hermitian tridiagonal and $E$ is a random diagonal matrix with independent absolutely continuous entries, then $gap(A+delta E) C(delta/n)^c$ for some constants $C,c$ depending on the distribution of the entries. Give an efficient deterministic algorithm for finding such a perturbation. Here, efficient means faster than the parent algorithm in which it is used, so $O(n^3 ^c(n/delta))$ for diagonalization and, ambitiously, $O(nnz(A) ^c(n/delta))$ or $O(nnz(A) ^c(n)/delta^c)$ for Krylov methods.

evidence.quote: Minami \cite{minami1996local} showed that if $A$ is $n\times n$ Hermitian tridiagonal and $E$ is a random diagonal matrix with independent absolutely continuous entries, then $gap(A+\delta E)\ge C(\delta/n)^c$ for some constants $C,c$ depending on the distribution of the entries. Give an efficient deterministic algorithm for finding such a perturbation. Here, efficient means faster than the parent algorithm in which it is used, so $O(n^3\log^c(n/\delta))$ for diagonalization and, ambitiously, $O(nnz(A)\log^c(n/\delta))$ or $O(nnz(A)\log^c(n)/\delta^c)$ for Krylov methods.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ Hermitian tridiagonal matrix, and for a diagonal matrix $E=\mathrm{diag}(e_1,\dots,e_n)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ and a parameter $\delta>0$, define the perturbed matrix $A+\delta E$. Write $\mathrm{gap}(M):=\min_{i\neq j}|\lambda_i(M)-\lambda_j(M)|$ for the minimum eigenvalue gap of a Hermitian matrix $M$.

A theorem of Minami (1996) asserts that there exist absolute constants $C,c>0$ such that, when the entries $e_1,\dots,e_n$ are independent and absolutely continuous (e.g.\ uniform on $[-1,1]$), the random perturbation satisfies
$$\Pr\!\big[\mathrm{gap}(A+\delta E)\ \ge\ C(\delta/n)^c\big]\ \ge\ 1/2.$$

Problem. Design a deterministic algorithm which, given $A$ and $\delta>0$, outputs a diagonal matrix $E\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ with $\|E\|\le 1$ such that
$$\mathrm{gap}(A+\delta E)\ \ge\ C(\delta/n)^c$$
for some absolute constants $C,c>0$, and which runs in time
$$O\!\big(n^3\,\log^c(n/\delta)\big)$$
(matching the cost of dense Hermitian diagonalization), and, more ambitiously, in time
$$O\!\big(\mathrm{nnz}(A)\,\log^c(n/\delta)\big)\quad\text{or}\quad O\!\big(\mathrm{nnz}(A)\,\log^c(n)/\delta^c\big)$$
suitable for use inside Krylov-subspace eigensolvers, where $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ is the number of nonzero entries of $A$.
artifact.category_tag: Numerical linear algebra / spectral gap perturbations
artifact.status_search_result: No source located that supplies a deterministic algorithmic version of Minami's eigenvalue-gap perturbation lemma for Hermitian tridiagonal matrices at the requested complexity. Recent work on deterministic Hermitian eigensolvers (e.g., the ICALP 2025 deterministic complexity analysis based on Gu–Eisenstat divide-and-conquer with the FMM) addresses related deterministic eigenproblem questions but does not provide a deterministic Minami perturbation. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Deterministic Complexity Analysis of Hermitian Eigenproblems
status_evidence.snippet: Deterministic algorithm to compute all eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix in O(n^omega F(log(n/eps)) + n^2 polylog(n/eps)) bit operations; analyzes Gu–Eisenstat divide-and-conquer with FMM.
status_evidence.claim: Recent deterministic Hermitian eigensolver work does not supply a deterministic Minami-type perturbation matching the stated efficiency targets, suggesting the problem is still open.
